jobs.name: port-serein-working-waterfront-v5
jobs.prompt:
Use case: compositing.
Asset type: screenshot-based environment reference for Veyra, an inhabited futuristic sci-fi RPG.
INPUT 1 IS THE EDIT TARGET: an actual screenshot from the existing game. INPUT 2 IS A MATERIAL/WEAR REFERENCE ONLY: an established gritty woodland settlement. Do NOT transplant that settlement or its forest into the target scene.
Preserve the target screenshot's exact camera, horizon, terrain profile, mountain silhouettes, sky, lighting direction, vegetation forms and ground textures. Keep the existing engine rendering. Remove the upper-left debug HUD and fill it with matching scene. Work onto the source background plate; natural areas outside construction should remain unchanged. Keep the original aspect ratio.
Shared art direction: functional, gritty far-future places with decades of work and repairs. Anarchy Online is an atmospheric inspiration. Concrete masses, moderately detailed manufactured shells, inset dark mechanical forms, smooth modest bevels, readable futuristic silhouettes. Economical geometry suitable for reusable Blender modules and cleaned-up generated assets. Weathered gray and cream, faded institutional green, oxide red, dark steel, old ochre safety markings. Different construction generations and replacement panels interrupt uniformity. Place corrosion at seams, runoff below fittings, worn patches at use points; preserve material distinction. Detail through broad texture/roughness variations, decals, a few repair parts and clearly chosen props. No dense micro-greebles or spaghetti cabling. Technology remains unmistakably futuristic and operational.
People work and live here. Avoid a pristine resort, coordinated fresh prefab set, fantasy ruin, abandoned post-apocalypse, military battle scene, toy-like low poly, triangulated foliage/terrain, excessive neon, or a whole-image sepia filter. Daylight must stay as in the screenshot. Depth and material realism should match the existing environment. No labels, captions, watermark, frame or collage.
SCENE: Port Serein's working waterfront, a dense civilian coastal district.
Keep open sea across the left half, the beach curve and the far-right mountain ridge. Build the city into the right coastal slope and right-middle shoreline. Make the near waterfront architecture large enough to read as an actual place, with a walkable quay, a battered ferry/cargo terminal, warehouses and modest 4-7-storey concrete residential blocks rising behind them. A distinctive older telecommunications/civic tower has a heavy stepped silhouette and faded vertical color bands. This is a working port grown over generations.
Use an elevated transit viaduct of thick concrete piers and repeated beams climbing across the district; patched trackside enclosures and a short enclosed transit car give futuristic identity. Salt-streaked facades, dark strip windows, balcony slabs and occasional mismatched enclosed balconies. Small shops and stalls fit into shaded ground-floor arches and loading recesses; worn fabric or sheet-metal shades differ from stall to stall.
At the harbor edge: simple chunky loading cranes, modular cargo stacks, a moored squat futuristic coastal freighter, a small passenger shuttle with blunt smoothly beveled bodywork resting on landing gear. A few tiny port workers and travelers establish scale. Add one exposed utility run and a repaired section of seawall, old safety paint and visible loading access. Carefully selected infrastructure, not countless tiny props. Leave part of the beach and much of the sea visible.
The skyline should suggest recognizable civic life and industrial investment, with an older heavier district close to water and later additions above. Do not make a sleek all-white marina. Do not copy the woodland buildings. Preserve the original water rendering as far as possible, adding only contact/reflections needed for the new structures.

SCENE: an operational regional terraforming service yard on the open plain.
Preserve the scattered small trees and the entire right-hand mountain ridge. Add a broad industrial installation in the middle ground, with a worn service access running from lower center into the compound. This is a distinct scene from a town and from a single heroic tower.
Main machine: a long raised atmospheric exchange hall with three large dark louvered intake faces, supported by heavy concrete buttresses, linked by a simple elevated service spine to TWO unequal vertical heat-exchange towers. The towers have broad tapered silhouettes, large inset vents and a few external service platforms. One tower retains faded cream cladding while the other has substantial replaced oxide-red panels. A tall simple instrumentation mast and a faint trace of vapor indicate operation. These are futuristic atmospheric machines rather than a present-day oil refinery.
Foreground-middle ground: a low control building, a repair shed with a broad open bay, two horizontal pressure tanks, a few thick pipes bridging low supports, a parked maintenance crawler with an angular cab, and a handful of workers at normal adult scale. Keep the major shapes clean and buildable. One repair panel stands beside the shed. Gate barriers, worn hazard strips, patch-repaired concrete, rust streaks under pipe brackets, dust near traffic and a little standing water around service drains show continued use.
Make the installation feel essential, expensive and repeatedly maintained. At least half the surrounding plain remains open, with the original vegetation and terrain. Avoid the ornate ribbed round rocket-like tower from earlier studies; this is a horizontal industrial campus with two offset towers and accessible human work areas.

SCENE: a roadside freight stop at walking height in rolling dry grassland.
Preserve the low rolling hills, sparse original saplings and the clear blue sky from input 1. Create a worn road curving from the lower-left foreground through a small foreground-middle-ground service stop toward the right distance. Use only a narrow construction footprint; leave the foreground/right-side sapling and much of the original landscape visible.
Main visual subject near the LEFT side of the road: a squat futuristic freight tug parked on landing legs beside a compact raised cargo-transfer rack. It has a wedge-shaped dark green cab, a long blunt rectangular cargo deck, four shrouded lift pods with simple dark openings, and two strapped modular freight containers, one red and one weathered cream. Smooth modest bevels, chunky functional construction, old fleet paint, replaced access panels and dust. No glowing levitation effects.
Behind it is a low concrete-and-composite canteen and repair bay with an asymmetric projecting canopy. The original standardized shell has acquired a mismatched corrugated extension, faded painted sign panel and a separate power cabinet. A small open sheltered seating area has two travelers and a mechanic; one doorway has a utilitarian warm light. A battered route terminal, one utility pylon, a few reusable cargo crates, charging/service hoses and broad road markings make its function readable. Use only a few thick, simple connections.
Composition should feel like the player is approaching a place to stop on a long journey, close enough to see vehicle proportions and doorway scale. This is distinctly a freight stop, not another three-house village. Keep the source perspective and ground texture around the road. Grit comes from traffic wear, maintenance and improvised additions, with life and useful services still present.
